chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ali ibn Hisan al-Vaseti, who linked it up to Zurarah, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, from the reality of faith is that you prefer the truth even if it harms you, over the falsehood even if it benefits you, and that your tongue does not exceed your knowledge.
ai.seo_question: What are the two main characteristics of true faith according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to delineate the internal and external manifestations of *Iman*, emphasizing that true faith requires both moral courage in choosing truth despite personal cost and intellectual humility in speech. The second condition, 'not exceeding one's knowledge in speech,' is often interpreted by Shia scholars as a safeguard against *ghibah* (backbiting) and *kalam bi-ghayr 'ilm* (speaking without knowledge), ensuring that one's tongue remains a vessel of wisdom rather than error. This dual focus aligns with the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as an integral component of belief, linking ethical conduct directly to spiritual authenticity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-70 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ali ibn Hisan al-Vaseti, who linked it up to Zurarah, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) who said, “Two characteristics are due to true faith. The first one is that you prefer the truth over the false, even if it may be to your disadvantage. The second one is that what you say is not beyond your intellect.”
